# Chicago Education Digest
_Jul 27 – Aug 10, 2026_

> Covering: K-12 Education & Schools · Board of Education & Governance

## K-12 Education & Schools

Chicago Public Schools' (CPS) budget for the upcoming school year has been a central focus, with the Board of Education approving a nearly $10 billion spending plan. A significant point of contention within this budget is its reliance on an anticipated $150 million in additional state funding, which some reports indicate is not yet secured. While Mayor Johnson has pressed for this funding, statements from Illinois House Speaker Emanuel "Chris" Welch have suggested that a firm commitment for this specific amount was not made. Despite receiving an increase in state dollars overall, analyses suggest CPS continues to move further from achieving full funding adequacy.

In response to budget discussions, initial plans for staff furloughs were reversed, and while some layoffs were reported, the Chicago Teachers Union indicated that layoffs were reversed, with CPS confirming schools will open on time. However, details regarding the full reversal of all layoffs remain limited. Separately, questions have been raised by parents and board members regarding the effectiveness and oversight of a $38 million CPS program, with one report indicating it has not met expectations. On the operational front, CPS is expanding its Sustainable Community Schools program and the Whole School Safety Model, and there were reports of school supplies being discarded outside former Acero charter schools recently taken over by the district.

## Board of Education & Governance

The Chicago Board of Education recently approved an amended $10 billion budget for Chicago Public Schools, a decision that has generated significant discussion and concern. A key element of the approved budget is its reliance on an assumed $150 million in additional state funding that has not yet been formally secured or approved by the state legislature. This approach has drawn criticism from some board members, parents, and observers, who have expressed reservations about the financial risk and the district's ability to obtain these funds. While Illinois House Speaker Welch and Mayor Johnson have publicly committed to advocating for the additional state funding, Chicago Public Schools is reportedly exploring financing options to address the potential shortfall if the funds do not materialize.

A notable development within the budget approval process was the reversal of earlier plans for teacher layoffs, a move welcomed by the Chicago Teachers Union. This reversal, however, is directly tied to the assumption of the $150 million in state funding. Prior to the budget's passage, there were reports of Milwaukee Public Schools actively recruiting Chicago teachers facing potential job cuts, and concerns were raised about the impact of initial cuts on Latino high schools. Despite the ongoing funding uncertainties, CPS has stated that schools will open on time. Separately, questions have been raised by parents and board members regarding a $38 million CPS program.

In the broader context of governance, discussions continue regarding the upcoming transition to an elected school board. Several articles highlight what is at stake in the upcoming races and the challenges the new board will face. Notably, some school board races have seen incumbents running unopposed, and Mayor Johnson recently appointed a new member to fill a current vacancy on the Board of Education.
